questions.question: "Dashain" and "Tihar" are popular festivals of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dashain** and **Tihar** are the two most significant festivals celebrated in **Nepal**, marking cultural and religious importance in the country.
 
• Dashain, also known as **Vijaya Dashami**, symbolizes the victory of good over evil and is dedicated to the Goddess Durga.
 
• Tihar, also called the **Festival of Lights**, is a five-day celebration that honors various animals, brothers, and the Goddess Laxmi, the deity of wealth.
 
• Both festivals are widely celebrated by the **Hindu majority population** of Nepal, and they reflect Nepal's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Dashain typically falls in September-October, while Tihar occurs in October-November, based on the lunar calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dashain:**

 
 
• Dashain is observed for 15 days, with each day representing different rituals, including **Ghatasthapana**, **Phulpati**, and **Vijaya Dashami**.
 
• It signifies the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon **Mahishasura**.
 
• The festival is marked by family gatherings, animal sacrifices, and the receiving of **Tika (rice, yogurt, and vermilion)** from elders.
 
• It is a time for new clothes, feasts, and the renewal of family and community bonds.
 
 
 
• **Tihar:**
 
 
• Also known as **Yama Panchak**, Tihar honors animals like crows, dogs, and cows, recognizing their role in human life.
 
• The third day, **Laxmi Puja**, is the most celebrated, with people lighting oil lamps and decorating homes to welcome the Goddess of Wealth.
 
• The fifth day, known as **Bhai Tika**, strengthens the bond between brothers and sisters through rituals and gift exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Religious and Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Both festivals are rooted in **Hindu mythology**, with Dashain focusing on divine power and Tihar emphasizing familial and animal respect.
 
• They are also celebrated among Nepalese communities worldwide, showcasing Nepal's cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Public Celebrations:**
 
 
• During Dashain, public spaces, temples, and homes are adorned with decorations, while Tihar features extensive use of **oil lamps and rangolis**.
 
• Both festivals are declared public holidays in Nepal, ensuring nationwide participation.

questions.question: Right of a prisoner to speedy trial will be categorized in which of the following Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Life**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The right to a speedy trial is derived from **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution, which guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty.
 
• The Supreme Court of India has interpreted the **Right to Life** to include the right to a speedy trial as part of the broader concept of justice.
 
• This right ensures that no person is deprived of their liberty without due process and protects individuals from prolonged judicial delays.
 
• The landmark case **Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979)** established the principle that a speedy trial is an integral part of Article 21.
 
• The right to a speedy trial aims to prevent undue harassment and ensure fair justice for prisoners and accused individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It states, "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• It is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution and is enforceable in courts.
 
 
 
• **Hussainara Khatoon Case (1979):**
 
 
• This case highlighted the plight of undertrial prisoners languishing in jails for extended periods due to judicial delays.
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that the right to a speedy trial is a fundamental right under Article 21.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation of Article 21:**
 
 
• The scope of Article 21 has been expanded over time to include rights like the right to privacy, the right to a clean environment, and the right to legal aid, among others.
 
• These interpretations aim to ensure that life and liberty are meaningful and not restricted to mere physical existence.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Speedy Trial:**
 
 
• Prevents unnecessary detention of undertrial prisoners.
 
• Ensures efficient administration of justice and prevents backlog in courts.
 
• Protects the dignity and mental well-being of accused individuals.

questions.question: All natural earthquakes take place in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lithosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Natural earthquakes occur primarily in the **lithosphere**, which is the rigid outermost layer of the Earth.
 
• The lithosphere consists of the Earth's crust and the uppermost part of the mantle, where tectonic plates interact, leading to seismic activity.
 
• Earthquakes are caused by the sudden release of energy due to **movement along faults** or the interaction of tectonic plates.
 
• Most earthquakes are concentrated along tectonic plate boundaries, including **divergent, convergent, and transform boundaries**.
 
• The lithosphere is characterized by its brittle behavior, making it prone to fracturing and generating seismic waves during an earthquake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asthenosphere:**

 
 
• The asthenosphere lies below the lithosphere and is a semi-fluid layer of the mantle.
 
• It allows tectonic plates in the lithosphere to move over it but does not experience earthquakes due to its ductile nature.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Waves:**
 
 
• Earthquakes generate seismic waves, which are classified as **primary (P) waves, secondary (S) waves, and surface waves**.
 
• These waves are responsible for the shaking felt during an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Tectonic Plate Boundaries:**
 
 
• Earthquakes are most common along tectonic plate boundaries, including **subduction zones, fault lines, and rift zones**.
 
• The "Ring of Fire" in the Pacific Ocean is one of the most seismically active regions in the world.
 
 
 
• **Richter Scale:**
 
 
• The magnitude of an earthquake is measured using the Richter scale, which quantifies the energy released during an event.
 
• Significant earthquakes often register above 5.0 on this scale.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Safety:**
 
 
• Safety measures include drop, cover, and hold during shaking, and ensuring buildings are constructed to withstand seismic forces.
 
• Preparedness can significantly reduce casualties and damage during an earthquake.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Alexander invade Punjab and in which of the following years did he die?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**326 BC and 323 BC.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alexander invaded Punjab in **326 BC** during his military expedition to the Indian subcontinent, specifically targeting the region of the Indus River.
 
• The invasion marked the famous Battle of Hydaspes against King Porus, which took place near the Jhelum River in present-day Punjab.
 
• Alexander's death occurred in **323 BC** in Babylon, reportedly due to fever, possibly exacerbated by other health conditions or poisoning.
 
• The invasion and subsequent death of Alexander significantly influenced the historical and cultural dynamics between Greece and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His campaigns laid the foundation for Indo-Greek interactions and exchanges in art, philosophy, and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Hydaspes:**

 
 
• Fought in 326 BC between Alexander the Great and King Porus.
 
• Despite losing, King Porus impressed Alexander with his bravery and leadership, leading Alexander to reinstate him as a satrap.
 
• It was a turning point that marked Alexander's furthest expansion into the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Alexander’s Death:**
 
 
• Occurred in Babylon in 323 BC at the age of 32.
 
• The cause remains debated, with theories ranging from typhoid fever, malaria, alcohol poisoning, or assassination.
 
• His sudden death led to the fragmentation of his empire among his generals, known as the Diadochi.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Indian Culture:**
 
 
• Alexander introduced Hellenistic influences in art, architecture, and coinage in India.
 
• His campaigns facilitated cultural exchange and trade routes between Greece and India.
 
• The Indo-Greek kingdoms that emerged later were direct results of Alexander’s influence.
 
 
 
• **Alexander’s Legacy:**
 
 
• Known as one of history’s greatest military strategists and conquerors.
 
• His empire stretched from Greece to Egypt and as far as the Indus River in India.
 
• He is remembered for spreading Greek culture across his empire, a phenomenon known as Hellenization.

questions.question: In which of the following states is Aoleang Monyu celebrated, which is an ancient spring festival celebrated by all Konyaks in the month of April?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aoleang Monyu is an ancient spring festival celebrated by the Konyak tribe of Nagaland every year in the month of April.
 
• The festival marks the end of the agricultural season and the beginning of the new year for the Konyak community.
 
• Aoleang Monyu is a week-long celebration involving rituals, traditional dances, songs, and feasts to honor nature and the spirits.
 
• The Konyak tribe is one of the largest Naga ethnic groups, known for their rich culture and heritage.
 
• The festival promotes unity and social harmony among the Konyak community and provides an opportunity to showcase their traditional attire, ornaments, and practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Konyak Tribe:**

 
 
• The Konyaks are one of the 17 officially recognized Naga tribes in Nagaland.
 
• They are known for their distinct traditions, including facial tattoos and unique headgear adorned with feathers and animal bones.
 
• Historically, the Konyaks were skilled warriors and practiced headhunting until the early 20th century.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Nagaland:**
 
 
• Nagaland is a northeastern state in India, bordered by Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Myanmar.
 
• Kohima is the state capital, and Dimapur is the largest city and commercial hub.
 
• The state is known for its hilly terrain, dense forests, and vibrant tribal culture.
 
 
 
• **Other Famous Festivals in Nagaland:**
 
 
• Hornbill Festival: Known as the "Festival of Festivals," it is celebrated in December to showcase Naga culture and heritage.
 
• Moatsu Festival: Celebrated by the Ao tribe to mark the completion of the sowing season.
 
• Sekrenyi Festival: Celebrated by the Angami tribe to purify the body and soul and ensure good health and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tribal Festivals:**
 
 
• Tribal festivals like Aoleang Monyu help preserve the cultural identity and traditions of indigenous communities.
 
• They play a key role in fostering unity and social bonds among community members.
 
• These festivals also attract tourists, providing economic benefits to the region.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a private sector industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tata Iron and Steel Company**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO)**, now known as Tata Steel, is a private sector company in India.
 
• Founded in **1907 by Jamsetji Tata**, Tata Steel is one of the world's largest private steel manufacturers.
 
• Tata Steel operates independently of government control and is part of the **Tata Group**, a private conglomerate.
 
• It is headquartered in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, and has operations across multiple countries.
 
• Unlike public sector companies like the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Tata Steel is listed as a private enterprise, representing India's thriving private industrial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Enterprises**

 
 
• These are companies where the majority stake (51% or more) is owned by the government.
 
• Examples include Life Insurance Corporation (LIC), Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).
 
• They are primarily established to serve public interests and contribute to national development.
 
 
 
• **Private Sector Enterprises**
 
 
• These are owned, managed, and controlled by private individuals or corporations.
 
• Examples include Tata Steel, Reliance Industries, Infosys, and Wipro.
 
• Private companies focus on profit generation and operate in a competitive market environment.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Public and Private Sector**
 
 
• Ownership: Public sector is government-owned, while private sector is privately owned.
 
• Objective: Public sector focuses on welfare and development, while private sector aims at profitability.
 
• Examples: Public sector includes entities like ONGC, while private sector includes companies like Tata Group.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Private Sector in India**
 
 
• Drives economic growth through innovation and competitiveness.
 
• Provides employment opportunities to a large section of the population.
 
• Plays a key role in the globalization of Indian industries, contributing to exports and foreign investments.

questions.question: Which specific chemical can be applied to achieve staining of chromosomes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetocarmine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acetocarmine** is a widely used stain for chromosomes, particularly in cytogenetic studies.
 
• It is prepared by dissolving carmine in acetic acid, which enhances its ability to bind chromosomal material.
 
• This stain highlights chromosomes by binding strongly to their DNA and proteins, making them visible under a microscope.
 
• Acetocarmine is commonly used for studying mitosis and meiosis in plant and animal cells.
 
• Its application enables researchers to analyze chromosomal structure and behavior during cell division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cytogenetics:** It is the study of chromosomes, their structure, and their function in relation to genetics.
 
• **Chromosome Staining:** Staining techniques, including acetocarmine and orcein, help visualize chromosomes for karyotyping and genetic analysis.
 
• **Mitosis and Meiosis:** These are fundamental processes of cell division where staining techniques play a critical role in observing chromosomal dynamics.
 
• **Carmine:** A natural dye extracted from cochineal insects, used to prepare acetocarmine and other biological stains.
 
• **Acetic Acid:** A vital component of acetocarmine, which aids in fixing and preserving cellular structures for microscopic examination.

questions.question: Which chronicler of the medieval age recognised that Raziyya was more able and qualified than all her brothers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minhaj-i-Siraj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Minhaj-i-Siraj, a 13th-century Persian historian and chronicler, acknowledged Raziyya Sultan's exceptional abilities and qualifications, comparing her favorably to her male siblings.
 
• In his work **"Tabaqat-i Nasiri"**, Minhaj-i-Siraj praised Raziyya for her administrative skills and leadership qualities.
 
• Raziyya Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate (1236-1240), belonging to the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• Despite societal norms against female leadership, Raziyya's merit was recognized by contemporary scholars like Minhaj-i-Siraj, who noted her capability to rule effectively.
 
• Minhaj-i-Siraj's writings are considered one of the primary historical sources for understanding Raziyya Sultan's reign and the challenges she faced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raziyya Sultan:**

 
 
• Raziyya Sultan ruled from 1236 to 1240 and was the daughter of Iltutmish, the third ruler of the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• She broke gender barriers by adopting male attire and titles to assert her authority in a patriarchal society.
 
• Raziyya was known for her reforms in administration, fostering trade, and promoting education and culture during her reign.
 
 
 
• **Minhaj-i-Siraj's "Tabaqat-i Nasiri":**
 
 
• This historical text is a detailed account of the rulers of the Islamic world, particularly the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the socio-political conditions of medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Mamluk Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Mamluk dynasty (1206–1290) was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Qutb al-Din Aibak.
 
• It was also known as the Slave Dynasty, as many rulers, including Raziyya Sultan's father Iltutmish, were former slaves who rose to power.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by Raziyya:**
 
 
• Raziyya faced strong opposition from nobles and courtiers who were unwilling to accept a female ruler.
 
• Her reign ended in 1240 after being deposed and eventually killed in a power struggle.

questions.question:
If after being bitten by a mosquito, the person is detected as being malaria positive, which of the following will hold true?

A. The person did not have a balanced diet.

B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.

C. The mosquito was suffering from malaria.

D. The person was not vaccinated as a child.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Malaria is caused by **Plasmodium parasites**, which are transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• The mosquito acts as the **vector** for the Plasmodium parasite, carrying and transmitting it to humans during a blood meal.
 
• Only female Anopheles mosquitoes are capable of transmitting malaria because they require blood to produce eggs.
 
• Plasmodium parasites include several species, such as **P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, and P. ovale**, with P. falciparum being the most deadly.
 
• Without the presence of Plasmodium in the mosquito, a mosquito bite does not result in malaria transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium Life Cycle:**

 
 
• Plasmodium parasites undergo a complex life cycle involving both humans and mosquitoes.
 
• The parasite's **sporozoites** are injected into the human bloodstream during a mosquito bite.
 
• In humans, the parasite first infects the liver before moving to red blood cells, causing the symptoms of malaria.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Malaria:**
 
 
• Common symptoms include fever, chills, headache, nausea, and muscle pain.
 
• Severe malaria can result in complications such as organ failure, cerebral malaria, or death.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Malaria:**
 
 
• Use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets (ITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS) can reduce mosquito exposure.
 
• Preventive medications, such as antimalarial drugs, are recommended for travelers to malaria-endemic areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Malaria Control Efforts:**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) leads initiatives like the **Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030** to reduce malaria cases and deaths.
 
• Malaria vaccine research, such as the RTS,S vaccine, is progressing as a potential tool for prevention.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian tribal dances is prevalent in the Araku Valley near Visakhapatnam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhimsa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhimsa** is a traditional tribal dance form performed by the **tribal communities of Andhra Pradesh**, specifically in the Araku Valley near Visakhapatnam.
 
• This dance is performed by tribal women dressed in colorful sarees and ornaments, moving rhythmically in a circular formation.
 
• **Dhimsa** is a representation of tribal culture and is performed during festivals, celebrations, and other community gatherings.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional tribal musical instruments like **dappu** (a type of drum) and other percussive instruments.
 
• Dhimsa reflects the simplicity, unity, and joy of tribal life and is a way of expressing gratitude to nature and their deities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Araku Valley**

 
 
• Located in the Visakhapatnam district of Andhra Pradesh, the Araku Valley is a scenic hill station known for its coffee plantations and tribal heritage.
 
• The region is home to several tribal communities, including the **Bagata, Kondadora, and Nookadora**.
 
• Araku is famous for its rich biodiversity and traditional practices, making it a hub of tribal art and culture.
 
 
 
• **Bagurumba**
 
 
• This is a popular folk dance of the Bodo tribe in Assam, performed by women during the Bwisagu festival.
 
• Bagurumba is characterized by graceful movements resembling nature, such as butterflies and birds.
 
 
 
• **Jhumur**
 
 
• Jhumur is a traditional dance performed in parts of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, often by tea garden workers.
 
• The dance is accompanied by folk songs and traditional instruments like the Mandar and Dhol.
 
 
 
• **Bardo Chham**
 
 
• Bardo Chham is a traditional dance of the Sherdukpen tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It depicts the victory of good over evil through elaborate costumes and masks representing animals and spirits.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution has provisions for the appointment of High Court Judges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 217**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 217 of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the **appointment and conditions of the office of High Court Judges**.
 
• The President of India appoints High Court Judges after consultation with the **Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the respective state, and the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court**.
 
• A person is qualified for appointment as a High Court Judge if they have served as an advocate in a High Court for at least **10 years** or have held judicial office in India for the same duration.
 
• The retirement age of a High Court Judge is **62 years**, as per the provisions under Article 217.
 
• The procedure for removal of High Court Judges is the same as for Supreme Court Judges and is governed by **Article 124(4) of the Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Court in India:**

 
 
• Each state in India has its own High Court, which acts as the highest judicial authority within the state.
 
• The High Court has original, appellate, and writ jurisdiction under the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Collegium System:**
 
 
• The appointment of High Court Judges involves the **Collegium System**, where senior judges of the Supreme Court recommend names to the President.
 
• This system ensures judicial independence and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• High Courts have the power of judicial review under Article 226, enabling them to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive actions.
 
• This is a crucial function to uphold the principles of justice and the rule of law.
 
 
 
• **Removal of Judges:**
 
 
• High Court Judges can be removed only through impeachment by Parliament, as per the procedure outlined in the Judges Inquiry Act, 1968.
 
• This ensures that removal is not arbitrary and is conducted with due process.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the principle laid down by the OECD about budgetary governance?

options.text: It does not allow the citizen to participate in budgetary debates.
The execution of the budget must be proactively planned, managed, and monitored.
Design the capital budgeting framework to meet national development needs.
Alignment of budgets with medium-term strategic priorities of the government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It does not allow the citizen to participate in budgetary debates.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The OECD principles on budgetary governance emphasize **transparency and citizen engagement** in the budgetary process.
 
• These principles advocate for **open, inclusive, and participatory mechanisms** to ensure public engagement and accountability.
 
• Citizen participation in budgetary debates is a fundamental component to ensure that budgetary policies reflect public priorities.
 
• The incorrect statement contradicts the OECD framework, as it suggests that citizens are restricted from participation, which is not aligned with the OECD's emphasis on inclusiveness.
 
• Other principles include strategic alignment of budgets, proactive planning and monitoring, and frameworks for capital budgeting to meet national development goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OECD Principles of Budgetary Governance:**

 
 
• Adopt a medium-term perspective in budgeting to align with strategic government priorities.
 
• Ensure budget transparency and open data to facilitate public scrutiny.
 
• Design a capital budgeting framework for sustainable and growth-oriented investments.
 
• Continuously monitor and evaluate budget outcomes to improve efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Citizen Engagement in Budgeting:**
 
 
• Public participation ensures alignment of budgetary policies with societal needs.
 
• Tools like participatory budgeting and public consultations are widely employed globally.
 
• Inclusive budgeting strengthens trust and accountability in governance.
 
 
 
• **Capital Budgeting Framework:**
 
 
• Focuses on long-term projects like infrastructure development and public utilities.
 
• Ensures that projects are aligned with national development plans and economic sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Budget Alignment:**
 
 
• Budgets should reflect medium-term priorities and policy goals of the government.
 
• Helps in efficient allocation of resources across different sectors.

questions.question: In February 2024, who was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ritu Bahri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Justice **Ritu Bahri** was sworn in as the first woman Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court in **February 2024**.
 
• She is a distinguished judge who previously served at the **Punjab and Haryana High Court**.
 
• Justice Ritu Bahri brings decades of judicial experience and expertise to her new role as Chief Justice.
 
• The appointment of Justice Bahri marks a significant milestone in gender representation within the Indian judiciary.
 
• Her elevation is in line with efforts to ensure greater diversity and inclusivity in higher judicial positions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uttarakhand High Court:**

 
 
• Established in **2000**, following the creation of the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• Located in **Nainital**, it handles cases pertaining to the state and exercises jurisdiction over civil, criminal, and constitutional matters.
 
 
 
• **Women in Indian Judiciary:**
 
 
• Justice **Fathima Beevi** was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India, appointed in 1989.
 
• Efforts are being made to increase the representation of women in higher judicial positions, including appointments of women Chief Justices.
 
 
 
• **Role of a Chief Justice:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is responsible for the administrative and judicial functioning of the court.
 
• They ensure fair hearings, timely disposal of cases, and adherence to constitutional values.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Appointments in India:**
 
 
• High Court judges are appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the respective state.
 
• The process emphasizes merit, seniority, and integrity.

questions.question: Which of the following countries won the maximum number of T20 Women's Cricket World Cup titles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Australia** is the most successful team in the history of the ICC T20 Women's Cricket World Cup.
 
• As of 2023, Australia has won the title **6 times** (2010, 2012, 2014, 2018, 2020, and 2023).
 
• The Australian Women's Cricket Team has consistently dominated international cricket with their exceptional performance and strong team dynamics.
 
• Australia's victory in the 2023 edition was a testament to their superior cricketing skills, defeating South Africa in the final.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts provided for a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Trade Disputes Act, 1929**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Trade Disputes Act, 1929**, was enacted to address industrial disputes and prevent their escalation into strikes or lockouts.
 
• The Act introduced a system of **industrial tribunals** to arbitrate disputes between employers and employees.
 
• It imposed a strict **ban on strikes** and lockouts in public utility services unless a notice was issued well in advance.
 
• The Act aimed to create a framework for resolving trade disputes through conciliation and arbitration rather than disruptive industrial actions.
 
• This legislation was one of the earliest measures by the British government in India to regulate labor relations and address the growing unrest among workers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947**

 
 
• This Act replaced the Trade Disputes Act, 1929, and became the cornerstone of labor dispute resolution in independent India.
 
• It introduced mechanisms such as conciliation officers, boards of conciliation, labor courts, and tribunals for dispute resolution.
 
• The Act also defined key terms such as "strike," "lockout," "retrenchment," and "layoff."
 
 
 
• **Strikes and Lockouts**
 
 
• A **strike** is a collective refusal by employees to work, usually to press for demands such as better wages or working conditions.
 
• A **lockout** is a temporary work stoppage or denial of employment initiated by the employer during a dispute.
 
 
 
• **Tribunals**
 
 
• Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies established to resolve specific types of disputes, including those related to labor and trade.
 
• They provide an alternative to traditional court systems, offering quicker and more specialized resolutions.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Trade Disputes Act, 1929**
 
 
• The Act was criticized for being biased toward employers, as it restricted workers' ability to strike.
 
• Despite its limitations, it laid the foundation for future labor legislation in India, focusing on industrial harmony and dispute resolution.

questions.question: Which of the following fields is NOT covered by the National Eminence Award?

• The award does not specifically cover the field of **Literature**, as it primarily focuses on the performing arts.
 
• Recipients of the award are selected for their exceptional dedication and lifelong achievements in their respective fields of performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**

• The Akademi aims to preserve and promote India's cultural heritage in performing arts.
 
• Apart from awards, it conducts research, documentation, and the publication of materials related to performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Fields of Recognition:**
 
 
• The awards focus on Theatre, Music (Hindustani, Carnatic, and folk traditions), and Dance (classical and traditional forms).
 
• It also includes allied performing arts, puppetry, and the contribution of scholars and teachers in these fields.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Award:**

questions.question: Carnatic singer Bombay Jayashri has been selected for which music award in 2023?

__
 
• The prestigious **Sangita Kalanidhi Award** is conferred by the Madras Music Academy, one of the most prominent institutions for Carnatic music.
 
• **Bombay Jayashri**, a renowned Carnatic vocalist, was selected for the Sangita Kalanidhi award in 2023 for her immense contributions to the field of classical music.
 
• The award is regarded as one of the highest honors in the world of Carnatic music and is given annually to a distinguished musician.
 
• Bombay Jayashri is celebrated for her melodious voice, innovative approach to music, and her efforts to popularize Carnatic music globally.
 
• The award ceremony is traditionally held during the Madras Music Academy's annual Margazhi festival in Chennai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bombay Jayashri:**

 
 
• She is a Padma Shri awardee and has an illustrious career spanning over decades in Carnatic music and film music.
 
• Her works include collaborations with musicians from various genres, including Hindustani music and global classical traditions.
 
• She is also known for her playback singing, having contributed to films like the Oscar-winning "Life of Pi."
 
• Her efforts include spreading awareness about Indian classical music through workshops, lectures, and performances worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Madras Music Academy:**

• The Sangita Kalanidhi award was instituted in 1942 and is given to individuals who have made outstanding contributions to Carnatic music.
 
• The academy conducts the annual Margazhi music festival, a significant cultural event in Chennai, attracting artists and audiences globally.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Carnatic music is a classical music tradition of South India, characterized by its complex compositions and improvisational elements.
 
• Key components include ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It is traditionally performed in a kutcheri (concert) format, with vocalists often accompanied by instruments such as the violin, mridangam, and tambura.

• Sangeetha Kalasarathy: Presented by Parthasarathy Swami Sabha for outstanding contributions to music.
 
• Sangeetha Kalasikhamani: Conferred by The Indian Fine Arts Society for lifetime achievements in music.

questions.question: Epic Poem, Savitri, described by its author as 'A Legend and a Symbol', was written by _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Epic Poem Savitri** is considered one of the greatest works of **Sri Aurobindo Ghosh**, often described as a spiritual and philosophical masterpiece.
 
• Sri Aurobindo referred to **Savitri** as "A Legend and a Symbol," which is a reflective interpretation of the eternal human quest for spiritual realization.
 
• The poem is composed of **12 books and 49 cantos**, covering over 23,000 lines, making it one of the longest epic poems in English literature.
 
• It is based on the **mythological story of Savitri and Satyavan** from the Mahabharata, reinterpreted as a metaphor for the transformation of human consciousness.
 
• The work encapsulates Sri Aurobindo's vision of the Divine Life on Earth and is deeply rooted in his philosophy of Integral Yoga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sri Aurobindo Ghosh** (1872–1950) was a philosopher, poet, nationalist, and spiritual reformer who played a significant role in India's independence movement before dedicating his life to spiritual pursuits.
 
• His philosophy of **Integral Yoga** emphasizes the synthesis of physical, mental, and spiritual evolution to create a divine life on Earth.
 
• The story of Savitri and Satyavan from the Mahabharata symbolizes **human resilience, devotion, and the conquest of death through love and divine intervention.**
 
• Sri Aurobindo's poetic style in Savitri is marked by its spiritual depth, symbolic imagery, and philosophical insights, making it a unique contribution to world literature.
 
• His works, including **The Life Divine**, **Essays on the Gita**, and **Savitri**, reflect his vision of spiritual evolution and the integration of the material and spiritual worlds.

questions.question: ‘Once a Dancer’ is the autobiography of ________________.

__
 
• **Allegra Kent** is a renowned American ballet dancer and writer, best known for her work with the New York City Ballet.
 
• Her autobiography, *Once a Dancer*, was published in **1997**, detailing her extraordinary life and career in ballet.
 
• Allegra Kent was a muse to **George Balanchine**, one of the greatest choreographers of the 20th century.
 
• She performed in iconic ballets such as *The Nutcracker*, *Agon*, and *Jewels*, leaving a lasting legacy in the world of dance.

• **Ballet Terminology**
 
 
• **Pas de Deux:** A dance duet performed by two dancers, typically a male and a female.

questions.question: Which track and field event has a water jump?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steeplechase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Steeplechase** is an athletics event that involves running and hurdling over obstacles, including a water jump.
 
• The water jump is a pit filled with water, positioned immediately after a hurdle, requiring athletes to leap over both the hurdle and the water.
 
• It is predominantly run over a distance of **3000 meters** in international competitions.
 
• The event is derived from horse racing and was first introduced in the athletics program at the **1900 Paris Olympics**.
 
• It is a test of endurance, speed, and agility, with athletes needing to clear a total of **28 hurdles** and **7 water jumps** during the race.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Steeplechase:**

 
 
• The event originated in Ireland, where horse races involved jumping over streams and stone walls between steeples of churches.
 
• The transition to human athletics began in the mid-19th century in England.
 
 
 
• **Water Jump Design:**
 
 
• The water pit is approximately **3.66 meters (12 feet) long** and slopes upward from a depth of **70 centimeters (28 inches)** at the base.
 
• Athletes must use momentum and technique to minimize contact with water and maintain speed.
 
 
 
• **Famous Athletes:**
 
 
• Kenyan runners have traditionally dominated the steeplechase, with legends like **Ezekiel Kemboi** and **Conseslus Kipruto** winning multiple Olympic and World Championship titles.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Events:**
 
 
• Unlike hurdles or decathlon, steeplechase uniquely includes water obstacles, adding complexity to the race.
 
• Cross-country running lacks artificial obstacles and is conducted over natural terrains.

questions.question: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plum Pudding Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• J.J. Thomson proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in 1898 after his discovery of the electron in 1897.
 
• According to this model, the atom is composed of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it, resembling a "plum pudding."
 
• The model suggested that the positive charge is uniformly distributed throughout the atom, balancing the negative charge of the electrons.
 
• It was the first model to include the electron, an important step in understanding atomic structure.
 
• This model was later disproved by Ernest Rutherford’s Gold Foil Experiment in 1909, which led to the discovery of the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Discovery:**

 
 
• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through his experiments with cathode rays.
 
• This discovery established that atoms are divisible and contain smaller subatomic particles.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• In 1909, Ernest Rutherford conducted the Gold Foil Experiment, which demonstrated that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• This experiment invalidated the Plum Pudding Model, leading to the Nuclear Model of the atom.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Model Evolution:**
 
 
• The Plum Pudding Model was an early attempt to explain atomic structure but lacked experimental support for the arrangement of charges.
 
• It was followed by Rutherford’s Nuclear Model and later by Niels Bohr’s Planetary Model.
 
 
 
• **Modern Atomic Theory:**
 
 
• The current understanding of atomic structure is based on quantum mechanics, incorporating the wave-particle duality of electrons and probabilistic electron clouds.

questions.question: Who excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Marshall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **John Marshall** was the Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) from 1902 to 1928.
 
• He is credited with initiating and overseeing the excavation of several significant historical sites, including **the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila**.
 
• The Chira Tope stupa, located in Taxila (modern-day Pakistan), is a Buddhist religious site linked to the Gandhara civilization.
 
• Marshall's work at Taxila was instrumental in uncovering its rich cultural heritage, including Buddhist stupas, monasteries, and ancient artifacts.
 
• His contributions to archaeology, particularly in South Asia, earned him recognition as one of the most important figures in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taxila:**

 
 
• An ancient city and a center of learning in the Gandhara region, Taxila is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It dates back to the 6th century BCE and was a hub of Buddhist culture and education.
 
• Taxila played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
 
 
• **John Marshall’s Contributions:**
 
 
• He was instrumental in excavating other key sites, such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, which led to the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• He emphasized the importance of systematic and scientific excavation techniques in archaeology.
 
 
 
• **Gandhara Art:**
 
 
• The Gandhara region, including Taxila, is famous for its unique art style that combines Indian and Greco-Roman influences.
 
• The art often depicts Buddhist themes and is characterized by intricate sculptures of the Buddha and bodhisattvas.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):**
 
 
• Established in 1861, ASI is responsible for the preservation and excavation of India's cultural and historical heritage.
 
• Under John Marshall's leadership, ASI made groundbreaking discoveries, laying the foundation for modern archaeology in India.

questions.question: The Zaskar and the Nubra are tributaries of which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Zaskar River** is a tributary of the Indus River, originating in the Zaskar Range of Ladakh, India.
 
• The **Nubra River**, also known as the Siachen River, is another tributary of the Indus, flowing through the Nubra Valley in Ladakh.
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, originating from the **Tibetan Plateau near Lake Mansarovar** and flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• Both Zaskar and Nubra rivers contribute significantly to the Indus River system, which supports agriculture, hydropower, and ecosystems in the region.
 
• The Indus River plays a crucial role in the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's earliest urban cultures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River System:**

 
 
• The Indus River spans approximately 3,180 km and flows through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• Major tributaries of the Indus include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, Zaskar, and Nubra.
 
• The river is vital for the Indus Basin Irrigation System, one of the largest irrigation networks globally.
 
 
 
• **Zaskar River:**
 
 
• The Zaskar River originates from the Zaskar Range and is known for its extreme conditions, including frozen river treks (Chadar Trek).
 
• It joins the Indus River near the town of Nimmu in Ladakh.
 
 
 
• **Nubra River:**
 
 
• The Nubra River originates from the Siachen Glacier, the world's second-largest glacier outside the polar regions.
 
• It flows into the Shyok River, which eventually merges with the Indus River.
 
 
 
• **Indus Waters Treaty (1960):**
 
 
• A water-distribution agreement between India and Pakistan, brokered by the World Bank.
 
• It allocates the waters of the Indus and its tributaries between the two countries, ensuring peaceful sharing.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the population density of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**382/km²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, the population density of India is **382 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of people living per square kilometer of land area.
 
• The population density of India in 2011 showed an increase from **325 persons per km² in 2001**, signifying a growth in population over the decade.
 
• Among Indian states, **Bihar** recorded the highest population density with **1,106 persons per km²**, while **Arunachal Pradesh** had the lowest density with just **17 persons per km²**.
 
• The high population density in certain regions is attributed to better economic opportunities, fertile land, and urbanization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Population Density**

 
 
• Population density is a measure of the number of people living in a unit area of land, usually expressed as persons per km².
 
• It provides insight into the spatial distribution of a population and helps in planning resource allocation and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Census of India 2011**
 
 
• It was the 15th Indian Census since 1872 and the 7th after independence.
 
• The total population of India as per the 2011 Census was **1.21 billion**, an increase of 181 million from the 2001 Census.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization and Population Density**
 
 
• Urban areas in India, such as Delhi and Mumbai, have significantly higher population densities compared to rural areas.
 
• Urbanization is driven by factors like employment opportunities, better living standards, and access to healthcare and education.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison**
 
 
• India ranks among the countries with high population density globally, alongside countries like Bangladesh and South Korea.
 
• However, regions such as Russia and Canada have significantly lower population densities due to vast land areas and smaller populations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of High Population Density**
 
 
• High population density can lead to challenges such as overcrowding, strain on resources, environmental degradation, and infrastructure issues.
 
• Proper urban planning and sustainable development are crucial to address these challenges effectively.
